result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.select_last_nodes_created()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select the last N nodes that were created. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5743-L5785){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.select_last_nodes_created(n) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Selects nodes in reverse chronological order based on creation time. Useful for incremental graph building workflows where you want to work with recently added nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of most recently created nodes to select. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Select recently added nodes: ::: {#810a2f9d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .select_last_nodes_created(2) ) # C and D are selected (most recent) selected = graph.get_selected_node_ids() # Returns ['C', 'D'] selected ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [3, 4] ``` ::: :::
